AI.result: Models pre-trained via TST using only in-environment multimodal data achieve competitive results compared to generalist models (DINOv2, CLIP) pre-trained on massive Internet datasets. The study also reveals tradeoffs between specialization to the test environment and generalization to held-out spaces based on pre-training data composition.
AI.conclusion: Cross-modal learning from test-environment-specific data can effectively substitute for large-scale external datasets, suggesting a paradigm where data quantity is replaced by multimodal richness. However, there exists a tradeoff between environment specialization and out-of-distribution generalization.

title: Seeing the End at Step Zero: Accelerating Diffusion MLLMs via MLP Sparsity-Aware Truncation
summary: Diffusion Multimodal Large Language Models (DMLLMs) are highly effective for multimodal reasoning, yet their inference efficiency is significantly hindered by fixed-length generation constraints. Since the actual output length is unknown, output sequences are padded to a predefined maximum length, resulting in substantial redundant computation over unnecessary [EOS] tokens. In this work, we discover that DMLLMs implicitly reveal their valid semantic boundary at the very first denoising step through a distinct shift in MLP activation sparsity. Leveraging this observation, we propose Seer, a training-free framework that detects this boundary using a Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR)-based criterion and performs one-shot truncation of the redundant suffix for all subsequent computations. To preserve these theoretical gains during batched serving, Seer incorporates a hybrid execution strategy that maximizes throughput while seamlessly accommodating dynamic sequence lengths. Experimental results demonstrate that Seer effectively eliminates padding waste, accelerating throughput by up to $\sim$31$\times$. Across 9 benchmarks, Seer robustly maintains overall performance and even improves accuracy on complex visual tasks by mitigating noise leakage (e.g., DocVQA score increases from 63.52 to 63.66), offering a highly efficient, plug-and-play solution for DMLLM acceleration.

AI.tldr: Seer is a training-free framework that detects the semantic boundary in DMLLMs at the first denoising step via MLP activation sparsity shift, enabling one-shot truncation of redundant [EOS] padding and achieving up to ~31× throughput acceleration with maintained or improved performance.
AI.motivation: DMLLMs suffer from fixed-length generation constraints where output sequences are padded to a predefined maximum length, causing substantial redundant computation over unnecessary [EOS] tokens and significantly hindering inference efficiency.
AI.method: Seer detects the valid semantic boundary at the first denoising step by observing a distinct shift in MLP activation sparsity, applies a Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR)-based criterion for boundary detection, performs one-shot truncation of the redundant suffix, and uses a hybrid execution strategy for batched serving with dynamic sequence lengths.
AI.result: Accelerates throughput by up to ~31×; across 9 benchmarks, maintains overall performance and improves accuracy on complex visual tasks (e.g., DocVQA from 63.52 to 63.66) by mitigating noise leakage.
AI.conclusion: Seer offers a highly efficient, plug-and-play, training-free solution for DMLLM acceleration by effectively eliminating padding waste.

title: Probabilistic Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Estimating Heterogeneous Elastic Properties from Low-Resolution and Noisy Displacement Data
summary: Estimating spatially heterogeneous elastic properties from low-resolution displacement measurements is a severely ill-posed inverse elasticity problem because low resolution obscures spatial details needed to distinguish heterogeneous property variations, and small measurement perturbations or fitting errors are amplified through inverse estimation. Existing inverse methods often rely on high-fidelity observations and manually prespecified loss weights, limiting their adaptability and making them sensitive to noise and resolution degradation. We propose a Probabilistic Inverse Elasticity Physics-Informed Neural Network (PIE-PINN) framework for robust estimation of Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio from noisy, low-resolution displacement data. PIE-PINN models displacement observation, strain-discrepancy, and equilibrium residuals using Laplace distributions within a unified probabilistic model. To improve robustness, the framework combines a B-spline-guided displacement network with a hierarchical half-Cauchy model for displacement residual scales. The B-spline provides a smooth global representation of the displacement field, while the neural network correction captures local variations. The hierarchical scale model adaptively downweights severe displacement fitting errors, enabling more robust recovery of the latent mean displacement field. An alternating maximum-likelihood training strategy updates the mean through weighted residual minimization and updates the scales to adjust the loss weights. Systematic case studies across varying noise levels and observation resolutions demonstrate the robustness of PIE-PINN.

AI.tldr: PIE-PINN is a probabilistic physics-informed neural network framework that robustly estimates heterogeneous elastic properties (Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio) from noisy, low-resolution displacement data by combining B-spline-guided displacement networks, hierarchical half-Cauchy scale modeling, and alternating maximum-likelihood training.
AI.motivation: Existing inverse elasticity methods rely on high-fidelity observations and manually prespecified loss weights, which limits adaptability and makes them sensitive to noise and resolution degradation. Low-resolution displacement measurements severely ill-poses the problem by obscuring spatial details and amplifying small errors through inverse estimation.
AI.method: PIE-PINN models displacement observation, strain-discrepancy, and equilibrium residuals using Laplace distributions within a unified probabilistic model. It combines a B-spline-guided displacement network (smooth global representation) with neural network correction (local variations) and a hierarchical half-Cauchy model to adaptively downweight severe displacement fitting errors. An alternating maximum-likelihood training strategy updates the mean via weighted residual minimization and scales to adjust loss weights adaptively.
AI.result: Systematic case studies across varying noise levels and observation resolutions demonstrate the robustness of PIE-PINN for estimating Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio from noisy, low-resolution displacement data.
AI.conclusion: PIE-PINN provides a robust, adaptive framework for solving the ill-posed inverse elasticity problem under challenging conditions of high noise and low resolution, eliminating the need for manually prespecified loss weights.

title: AE-UAV: An Air-to-Air Event-Based UAV Tracking Benchmark and a Real-Time Frequency-Domain Tracker
comment: 12 pages, 7 figures. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
summary: Air-to-air (A2A) unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) tracking is fundamental to airborne remote sensing of low-altitude aerial targets. However, the deployment of continuous, real-time tracking systems on UAVs presents significant challenges. In A2A scenarios, traditional frame-based cameras suffer from severe performance degradation under low illumination, overexposure, and high-speed motion owing to their limited dynamic range and fixed temporal sampling. Although event cameras offer a promising alternative with microsecond temporal resolution and a high dynamic range, current research is bottlenecked by two primary issues: 1) the absence of dedicated A2A event-based datasets, and 2) the heavy reliance of existing trackers on GPU acceleration and extensive training data, rendering them impractical for resource-constrained UAVs. To bridge these gaps, we introduce AE-UAV, an air-to-air event-based UAV tracking benchmark. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first airborne-captured event camera dataset for A2A tracking, comprising 178 flight sequences with continuous-time cubic B-spline annotations. Furthermore, we propose the Fast-Slow Frequency-domain Tracking (FSFT) method. This lightweight, training-free framework seamlessly integrates frequency-domain template matching with search region prediction and detection-based drift correction. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FSFT operates at an ultra-fast 420 frames per second (FPS) on CPU-only hardware. It retains 93.97% of the accuracy of state-of-the-art GPU-dependent methods while delivering a 5.32-fold effective speedup and exhibiting superior temporal resolution generalization, thereby providing a highly efficient and robust solution for airborne remote sensing of aerial targets. The dataset and source code are available at https://github.com/MSP-xEN/AE-UAV.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces AE-UAV, the first airborne-captured event camera dataset for air-to-air UAV tracking, and proposes FSFT, a lightweight, training-free frequency-domain tracking framework that achieves 420 FPS on CPU-only hardware with 93.97% of the accuracy of GPU-dependent methods.
AI.motivation: Traditional frame-based cameras suffer from performance degradation in A2A UAV tracking under low illumination, overexposure, and high-speed motion due to limited dynamic range and fixed temporal sampling. Event cameras offer microsecond temporal resolution and high dynamic range, but current research lacks dedicated A2A event-based datasets and existing trackers rely heavily on GPU acceleration and extensive training data, making them impractical for resource-constrained UAVs.
AI.method: The authors create AE-UAV, a dataset with 178 flight sequences and continuous-time cubic B-spline annotations captured from airborne event cameras. They propose FSFT (Fast-Slow Frequency-domain Tracking), a lightweight, training-free framework that integrates frequency-domain template matching with search region prediction and detection-based drift correction.
AI.result: FSFT operates at 420 FPS on CPU-only hardware, retains 93.97% accuracy of state-of-the-art GPU-dependent methods, achieves 5.32-fold effective speedup, and demonstrates superior temporal resolution generalization.
AI.conclusion: The AE-UAV dataset and FSFT method provide a highly efficient and robust solution for airborne remote sensing of aerial targets, enabling real-time A2A UAV tracking on resource-constrained platforms without GPU dependency.

title: Democratizing Agent Deployment Safety: A Structural Monitoring Approach
comment: Accepted in ICML 2026 Workshops: AI4GOOD and AIWILD
summary: AI software development agents are increasingly capable of modifying infrastructure and security critical systems, creating risks where an agent completes its assigned task while covertly weakening safeguards through actions such as broadening permissions, degrading logging, or introducing persistence mechanisms. While frontier laboratories may deploy sophisticated monitoring pipelines, many organizations and individual users adopting coding agents lack the resources and governance maturity required to maintain complex learned monitor ensembles. We study this problem as infrastructure level sabotage under task success in the infrastructure-as-code setting from ControlArena and compare trained and untrained monitors across synchronous and asynchronous deployment modes. We introduce an Information Flow Graph (IFG) monitor that analyzes structural security regressions using control-flow and data-flow graph diffs alongside raw code diffs. In asynchronous evaluation, an untrained git diff monitor misses 11.6% attacks at 1% false positive rate auditing budget, our untrained IFG monitor reduces this to 3.5%, and the trained Async RF monitor achieves below 1%. Unlike the trained Async RF monitor, IFG can also operate synchronously as a pre-deployment safeguard that blocks suspicious infrastructure changes before execution or merge. In synchronous mode, IFG realtime rollback reduces joint main task and covert task success from 74.4% to 0.0% with no measurable reduction in legitimate task completion. These results suggest that untrained structural monitors provide a practical and auditable path toward democratizing deployment safety for organizations seeking trustworthy adoption of advanced AI agents.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces an Information Flow Graph (IFG) monitor for detecting infrastructure-level sabotage by AI coding agents. The IFG monitor analyzes structural security regressions via control-flow and data-flow graph diffs. In asynchronous mode, it reduces missed attacks from 11.6% (git diff) to 3.5% at 1% FPR; in synchronous mode, it reduces joint main+covert task success from 74.4% to 0.0% with no measurable impact on legitimate tasks.
AI.motivation: AI software development agents can modify infrastructure and security-critical systems, creating risks where agents complete tasks while covertly weakening safeguards (e.g., broadening permissions, degrading logging, introducing persistence). Many organizations lack resources for complex learned monitor ensembles used by frontier labs.
AI.method: The authors study infrastructure-level sabotage in the infrastructure-as-code setting from ControlArena. They propose an Information Flow Graph (IFG) monitor that analyzes structural security regressions using control-flow and data-flow graph diffs alongside raw code diffs. They compare trained vs. untrained monitors across synchronous (pre-deployment) and asynchronous (post-hoc) deployment modes.
AI.result: Asynchronous: untrained git diff monitor misses 11.6% attacks (1% FPR); IFG monitor reduces misses to 3.5%; trained Async RF monitor achieves <1%. Synchronous: IFG realtime rollback reduces joint main+covert task success from 74.4% to 0.0% with no measurable reduction in legitimate task completion.
AI.conclusion: Untrained structural monitors (like IFG) provide a practical, auditable path toward democratizing deployment safety for organizations seeking trustworthy adoption of advanced AI agents.

title: Gate-Zero Growth: A Geometric Framework for Function-Preserving Continual Learning
summary: We introduce \emph{gate-zero growth}, a function-preserving (FP) operator for continual learning that adds new residual blocks through a zero-initialised gate. Under a transversality condition, gate-zero growth induces \emph{rank separation} in the functional Jacobian: old directions are unchanged, new-weight directions are exactly flat at the growth point, and new gate directions are the only first-order source of new functional variation. As gates open during continual learning, function drift is $O(\|\boldsymbolα\|^2)$ and Jacobian leakage $O(\|\boldsymbolα\|_\infty)$, giving a controlled departure from the FP locus. On a $300\mathrm{M}\to857\mathrm{M}$ Transformer adapted from WikiText-103 to BookCorpus, gate-zero growth reaches near-zero old-domain forgetting ($Δ_A < 0.1$) under both exact-preservation (Isolation) and joint-frontier (Freeze-Nothing) operating points, while a non-FP control ($G_{\text{stack}}$) suffers an order-of-magnitude larger forgetting under the same recipe. The same geometric analysis covers LoRA, ReZero, and zero-init adapter constructions, establishing gate-zero growth as the canonical instance of a shared local geometry that governs safe capacity activation in CL.

AI.tldr: Gate-zero growth is a function-preserving operator that adds residual blocks via zero-initialized gates, enabling continual learning with controlled function drift and Jacobian leakage. It achieves near-zero forgetting on a 300M→857M Transformer adaptation, outperforming non-FP baselines by an order of magnitude.
AI.motivation: To enable safe capacity expansion in continual learning without catastrophic forgetting, by introducing a function-preserving operator that ensures new parameters do not alter the existing model output at initialization.
AI.method: Gate-zero growth adds residual blocks through a zero-initialised gate. Under a transversality condition, it induces rank separation in the functional Jacobian: old directions unchanged, new-weight directions flat, new-gate directions provide first-order functional variation. Gates open gradually; function drift is O(‖α‖²) and Jacobian leakage O(‖α‖_∞).
AI.result: On a 300M→857M Transformer adapted from WikiText-103 to BookCorpus, gate-zero growth achieves near-zero old-domain forgetting (Δ_A < 0.1) under both Isolation and Freeze-Nothing regimes, while a non-FP control (G_stack) suffers an order-of-magnitude larger forgetting.
AI.conclusion: Gate-zero growth is the canonical instance of a shared local geometry (covering LoRA, ReZero, zero-init adapters) that governs safe capacity activation in continual learning.

title: WorkDrive: Roadwork Chain of Causation for Autonomous Driving
summary: Autonomous driving vision-language models (VLMs) struggle in roadwork zones, where familiar visual cues such as lane markings and permanent signs are altered or absent, and temporary devices such as cones and barriers redefine the drivable corridor. VLMs can detect these objects, but without explicit guidance they anchor their reasoning on familiar elements from pre-training and fail to connect work-zone observations to correct planning decisions. We propose WorkDrive, a framework that constructs perception-grounded causal reasoning for work zones and aligns it with trajectory prediction. An automated multitask perception pipeline extracts structured scene facts and injects them into a Chain-of-Causation (CoC) annotation pipeline, redirecting the annotator's attention to domain-specific elements. The resulting reasoning labels are used for supervised fine-tuning, followed by reinforcement learning with a single reward: consistency between lateral meta-actions and the predicted trajectory. On ROADWork, the largest public work-zone dataset, the proposed roadwork CoC reduces trajectory average displacement error (ADE) by 9.0\%, and consistency-based GRPO yields a further 3.0\%, achieving progressive improvement over the trajectory-only baseline. Code and data will be publicly released.

AI.tldr: WorkDrive is a framework that enhances autonomous driving VLMs for roadwork zones by using perception-grounded causal reasoning (Chain-of-Causation) and consistency-based reinforcement learning, achieving 12% ADE reduction on the ROADWork dataset.
AI.motivation: Autonomous driving VLMs perform poorly in roadwork zones because familiar visual cues (lane markings, signs) are altered or absent, and models anchor on pre-training knowledge rather than work-zone observations, leading to incorrect planning decisions.
AI.method: WorkDrive uses (1) an automated multitask perception pipeline to extract structured scene facts, (2) a Chain-of-Causation (CoC) annotation pipeline that redirects attention to domain-specific elements, (3) supervised fine-tuning with CoC reasoning labels, and (4) reinforcement learning (GRPO) with a single reward: consistency between lateral meta-actions and predicted trajectory.
AI.result: On the ROADWork dataset, roadwork CoC reduces ADE by 9.0%, and consistency-based GRPO yields a further 3.0% improvement, totaling 12% ADE reduction over the trajectory-only baseline.
AI.conclusion: Explicit causal reasoning grounded in perception, combined with action-trajectory consistency reinforcement, progressively improves trajectory prediction in challenging roadwork zones.

title: Sharp Stability Threshold and Certification for Designing Stable Residual Architectures
summary: We propose \emph{the sublinear-growth principle} for deep residual architectures -- a sharp stability threshold on the input-magnitude exponent of every residual block's velocity field: $$\|v(x, t)\| \leq c\,\|x\|^q + b, \qquad q \in [0, 1].$$ The threshold $q = 1$ is established via two independent arguments. Classical ODE theory gives a global forward flow on $[0, T]$ at $q \le 1$ and exhibits divergent velocity fields at any $q > 1$. The optimal-control analysis, via the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation, sharpens this to a selection statement: the training optimum is bang-bang on the boundary of the admissible class, so the optimum at $q > 1$ blows up while the optimum at $q \le 1$ is safe by construction. The exponent criterion $q \le 1$ is thereby a necessary and sufficient condition for stable training. It clarifies architectural placements that ensure the stability of training and inference, explaining, for instance, the stabilizing role of layer normalization. The sublinear-growth velocity fields form \emph{the right function space} on which forward dynamics, adjoint sensitivity, and architectural composition are all well-controlled. An arithmetic of input-magnitude exponents under the five operations that build residual blocks enables efficient certification of $q_k \le 1$ at the level of architectural primitives, in place of ad hoc trial and error in the search for stable neural architectural designs. A parameter-free modification reduces the supercritical Mamba block from $q = 5$ to $q = 1$ without layer normalization, demonstrating this point. Experiments on Mamba and PatchTST confirm that the $q \le 1$ variants train stably: the criterion is the input-magnitude exponent, not the presence of a normalization layer.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes the sublinear-growth principle for deep residual architectures, establishing that a residual block's velocity field must satisfy ∥v(x,t)∥ ≤ c∥x∥^q + b with q ≤ 1 for stable training. This threshold is proven via ODE theory and optimal control analysis, and an arithmetic of input-magnitude exponents enables efficient certification of stable architectural designs without relying on normalization layers.
AI.motivation: To identify a fundamental mathematical principle governing training stability in deep residual networks, replacing ad hoc trial-and-error approaches for neural architectural design.
AI.method: The paper uses classical ODE theory and Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman optimal control analysis to establish the q ≤ 1 threshold, and develops an arithmetic of input-magnitude exponents for architectural primitives to certify stability.
AI.result: The exponent criterion q ≤ 1 is a necessary and sufficient condition for stable training. A parameter-free modification reduces Mamba's exponent from q=5 to q=1 without layer normalization, and experiments on Mamba and PatchTST confirm stable training for q ≤ 1 variants.
AI.conclusion: The sublinear-growth principle defines the correct function space for well-controlled forward dynamics, adjoint sensitivity, and architectural composition. Input-magnitude exponent, not normalization layers, is the true determinant of training stability.

title: VQ-Touch: A Data-Efficient Tactile Generation Framework Across Sensors and Scenarios
summary: Tactile image generation significantly reduces the dependency on expensive and wear-prone sensors by synthesizing high-fidelity tactile data, offering an efficient solution for tactile information acquisition in robotic perception and human-machine interaction systems. However, existing methods depend on large-scale, diverse datasets from specific sensors and lack efficient data utilization and robust generalization capabilities, struggling in vision-limited environments. To address this, we introduce VQ-Touch, a tactile generation framework that supports both cross-sensor and multi-scenario applications. Specifically, to efficiently extract complex deformation and texture features from the data, we propose DM-VQGAN, an effective tactile representation learner. Furthermore, we introduce a discrete diffusion decoder with a unified conditioning interface, supporting multimodal generation tasks such as images and labels, and enhances the model's generalization capability through few-shot mixed training, thus achieving compatibility with current mainstream sensors and their variants. Experiments show that VQ-Touch surpasses state-of-the-art methods in multiple tasks.

AI.tldr: VQ-Touch is a tactile image generation framework that uses DM-VQGAN for tactile representation learning and a discrete diffusion decoder with unified conditioning to achieve cross-sensor and multi-scenario tactile generation, outperforming existing methods.
AI.motivation: Existing tactile generation methods depend on large-scale, diverse datasets from specific sensors, lack efficient data utilization and robust generalization, and struggle in vision-limited environments. There is a need for a more efficient and generalizable tactile generation approach.
AI.method: Proposes DM-VQGAN for efficient extraction of complex deformation and texture features; introduces a discrete diffusion decoder with a unified conditioning interface supporting multimodal generation (images, labels); employs few-shot mixed training to enhance generalization across sensors.
AI.result: VQ-Touch surpasses state-of-the-art methods in multiple tasks, demonstrating superior cross-sensor and multi-scenario performance.
AI.conclusion: VQ-Touch effectively addresses sensor dependency and generalization limitations in tactile generation, providing a compatible solution for mainstream sensors and their variants.

title: Collaborative Spatial Learning with Multi-LLM Agents in Networked Social Experiments
comment: Accepted at ASONAM 2026; to appear in the Springer proceedings
summary: Collective problem solving often requires that group members consider the tradeoff between exploitation of known solutions and exploration for new ones, where information of known solutions can be disseminated among individual members through communication networks. The Mason--Watts experiment (PNAS 2012) showed that human groups in shorter-path networks outperform those in longer-path networks on a two-dimensional search task. In this work, we focus on the investigation of such network-efficiency effects in the setting of a group of large language model (LLM) agents. Specifically, we consider groups of sixteen LLM agents playing the Mason--Watts experiment on the eight Mason--Watts network topologies. Moreover, we develop mechanistic Bayesian optimization agents such that the performance of LLM agents can be compared with both the mechanistic agents and the human experimental data. Our computational experiments indicate that the LLM agents show a significant network-efficiency effect when instructed to randomize their first-round choices, but not under the default initialization. In this experiment, adding a one-sentence first-round randomization instruction improves collective payoff by more than three times the estimated payoff difference across the eight network topologies. Also, the Bayesian optimization agents obtain higher payoffs than the evaluated LLM agents on this spatial search task. We further compare the agents' exploration--exploitation behavior, copying, and spatial diversity.

AI.tldr: LLM agents show network-efficiency effects in a collective spatial search task only when instructed to randomize first-round choices, with Bayesian optimization agents outperforming LLM agents.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether LLM agents exhibit network-efficiency effects (shorter-path networks leading to better collective performance) similar to humans in the Mason-Watts experiment, and to compare LLM agent behavior with mechanistic agents and human data.
AI.method: Groups of 16 LLM agents performed the Mason-Watts spatial search task across eight network topologies. First-round randomization instruction was tested. Bayesian optimization agents were developed as mechanistic baselines. Exploration-exploitation, copying behavior, and spatial diversity were analyzed.
AI.result: LLM agents showed significant network-efficiency effects only with first-round randomization instruction, which improved collective payoff by over 3x the payoff difference across topologies. Bayesian optimization agents outperformed LLM agents overall.
AI.conclusion: Network topology effects in LLM groups depend on initialization conditions; simple randomization instructions can substantially enhance collective performance in spatial search tasks.

title: Accelerating A/B-Tests with Counterfactual Estimation: Reducing Variance through Policy Overlap
summary:
Online controlled experiments are the gold standard for hypothesis testing in online platforms. Notwithstanding their ubiquity, they are notoriously expensive to run, and issues of variance hamper statistical power in assessing treatment effects. While standard variance reduction techniques leverage model-based control variates to reduce outcome noise, they remain agnostic to potential structural relationships between competing policies.
  In this work, we identify a critical inefficiency in the standard A/B-testing protocol: when a treatment and control policy agree on an action, the resulting outcome contributes noise but no signal regarding the treatment effect -- unnecessarily inflating confidence intervals. We propose a novel experimental protocol that exploits this policy overlap to accelerate experimentation. The key insight is to frame the randomised treatment assignment mechanism as a meta-policy, and leverage $Δ$-Off-Policy Estimation methods to obtain unbiased estimates for average treatment effects. We prove analytically that our approach recovers standard A/B-testing practices in the general case, but that its variance scales with the divergence between policies rather than raw outcome variance. Hence, we dominate the standard Difference-in-Means estimator whenever policies have common support, and the improvement is strict whenever the overlap region contributes non-zero residual variance. Empirical results corroborate these theoretical insights -- holding promise for significant impact on the real-world evaluation of recommender systems, information retrieval pipelines, and large language model interfaces.

AI.tldr: The paper identifies inefficiency in standard A/B-testing due to policy overlap (when treatment and control agree on actions, outcomes add noise but no signal). It proposes a new protocol using Δ-Off-Policy Estimation to obtain unbiased treatment effect estimates with variance scaling by policy divergence rather than raw outcome variance, dominating standard Difference-in-Means when policies share common support.
AI.motivation: Standard A/B-testing suffers from high variance and costly experimentation; existing variance reduction techniques ignore structural relationships between competing policies, leaving a critical inefficiency unaddressed.
AI.method: Frames the randomized treatment assignment mechanism as a meta-policy and leverages Δ-Off-Policy Estimation (Δ-OPE) methods to obtain unbiased estimates of average treatment effects by exploiting policy overlap regions.
AI.result: Variance scales with policy divergence rather than raw outcome variance; dominates Difference-in-Means estimator whenever policies have common support; strict improvement when overlap contributes non-zero residual variance. Empirical results corroborate theoretical insights.
AI.conclusion: The proposed protocol accelerates experimentation by eliminating noise from policy overlap, with significant implications for evaluating recommender systems, information retrieval pipelines, and large language model interfaces.

title: GeoDetect: Geometric Adversarial Detection for VLPs
summary: Vision-language pre-trained models (VLPs) are widely used in real-world applications. However, they remain vulnerable to adversarial attacks. Although adversarial detection methods have demonstrated success in single-modality settings (either vision or language), their effectiveness and reliability in multimodal models such as VLPs remain largely unexplored. In this work, we study the geometry of VLP embedding spaces and observe structured anisotropy that differs from unimodal vision models. Our theoretical analysis shows that under this anisotropic structure, adversarial attacks increase the expected geometric separation between clean and adversarial examples (AEs). Specifically, we demonstrate that AEs consistently exhibit greater expected distances to randomly sampled points than their clean counterparts, indicating that AEs tend to push representations out of manifold regions. Building on these insights, we propose GeoDetect, which leverages these off-manifold deviations via geometric scores to identify AEs. Through comprehensive evaluations, we show that our approach reliably detects AEs across diverse VLP architectures and threat settings, covering unimodal and multimodal attacks as well as adaptive attacks, thereby providing a robust and practical approach to improving the safety and reliability of these models.

AI.tldr: GeoDetect detects adversarial examples in vision-language pre-trained models by leveraging geometric properties of their embedding spaces, specifically the anisotropic structure that causes adversarial examples to deviate off-manifold.
AI.motivation: VLPs are vulnerable to adversarial attacks, but existing adversarial detection methods are designed for single-modality settings and their effectiveness in multimodal VLPs is unexplored.
AI.method: The authors study the geometry of VLP embedding spaces, observe structured anisotropy differing from unimodal vision models, and theoretically show that adversarial attacks increase expected geometric separation. They propose GeoDetect which uses geometric scores to identify off-manifold deviations of adversarial examples.
AI.result: GeoDetect reliably detects adversarial examples across diverse VLP architectures and threat settings, including unimodal, multimodal, and adaptive attacks.
AI.conclusion: Geometric detection leveraging anisotropic structure provides a robust and practical approach to improving safety and reliability of VLPs against adversarial attacks.

title: Multi-LLM Collaborative MRI Report Generation for Visual Instruction Tuning in Brain Oncology
summary: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) and their extension to vision-language models (VLMs) have made it easier to combine text and images for tasks such as report generation. Existing VLMs in medicine typically focus on 2D images (chest X-rays), and their extension to 3D imaging has been difficult because of the lack of paired 3D imaging-text data. Thus, we introduce a new method for creating a 3D image-text dataset for brain oncology using 3D MRI scans of glioma and meningioma cases. We use a cooperative system in which several LLMs work together to generate and check reports, ensuring that they are accurate and clear. By leveraging the new 3D MRI-text dataset, we further build a VLM that converts MRI scans into tokens and aligns them with text instructions. Our VLM performed better in report generation and visual question answering tasks than other 2D and 3D methods. Our method not only improves the quality of reports but also helps with better diagnosis and treatment in brain oncology.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a method to create a 3D MRI-text dataset for brain oncology (glioma and meningioma) using cooperative LLMs for report verification, and builds a VLM that aligns 3D MRI tokens with text instructions, outperforming existing 2D and 3D methods in report generation and visual question answering.
AI.motivation: Existing VLMs in medicine are limited to 2D images (e.g., chest X-rays) and struggle to extend to 3D imaging due to the scarcity of paired 3D imaging-text data, motivating the need for a 3D MRI-text dataset and a corresponding VLM for brain oncology.
AI.method: The method involves (1) creating a 3D MRI-text dataset for glioma and meningioma cases using a cooperative system of multiple LLMs that generate and verify reports for accuracy and clarity, and (2) building a VLM that converts 3D MRI scans into tokens and aligns them with text instructions for downstream tasks.
AI.result: The proposed VLM outperforms other 2D and 3D methods in both report generation and visual question answering tasks.
AI.conclusion: The method improves the quality of generated reports and contributes to better diagnosis and treatment in brain oncology.

title: Auditing Fairness-Privacy Trade-offs: Subpopulation-Level Effects of Fairness-Enhancing Algorithms
summary: Machine learning (ML) models deployed in sensitive domains such as healthcare, law enforcement, and finance must satisfy not only utility requirements but also fairness and privacy guarantees. While prior work has largely examined how privacy-preserving techniques affect fairness, the inverse question-how fairness-enhancing algorithms influence privacy leakage-remains underexplored. We present the first comprehensive study of how fairness interventions affect membership inference privacy risks at the subpopulation level. By adapting the Likelihood Ratio Attack (LiRA) for subgroup auditing, we uncover privacy disparities that aggregate evaluations obscure. We further analyze how Differential Privacy (DP) interacts with fairness-enhancing methods across different categories, showing that DP's privacy benefits and utility costs are unevenly distributed across subpopulations. Our results demonstrate that fairness interventions do not uniformly increase privacy risk; their impact depends on model architecture, subgroup size, and mitigation strategy. These findings reveal that fairness, privacy, and utility must be jointly evaluated at the subpopulation level, and we introduce the first unified empirical framework to support such auditing in practice.

AI.tldr: This paper systematically studies how fairness-enhancing algorithms affect membership inference privacy risks at the subpopulation level, revealing that fairness interventions do not uniformly increase privacy risk and introducing a unified empirical framework for joint auditing of fairness, privacy, and utility.
AI.motivation: While prior work has examined how privacy-preserving techniques affect fairness, the inverse question—how fairness-enhancing algorithms influence privacy leakage—remains underexplored, especially at the subpopulation level where aggregate evaluations may obscure disparities.
AI.method: The authors adapt the Likelihood Ratio Attack (LiRA) for subgroup auditing, analyze how Differential Privacy interacts with fairness-enhancing methods across different categories, and evaluate the impact of fairness interventions on membership inference risks considering model architecture, subgroup size, and mitigation strategy.
AI.result: Fairness interventions do not uniformly increase privacy risk; their impact varies based on model architecture, subgroup size, and mitigation strategy. DP's privacy benefits and utility costs are unevenly distributed across subpopulations, and privacy disparities exist that aggregate evaluations fail to capture.
AI.conclusion: Fairness, privacy, and utility must be jointly evaluated at the subpopulation level, and the paper introduces the first unified empirical framework to support such auditing in practice.

title: FoMoVLA: Bridging Visual Foresight and Motion Guidance for Vision-Language-Action Models
comment: 12 pages, 7 figures, 8 tables. Project page: https://liauto-research.github.io/FoMoVLA
summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have achieved impressive results in visuomotor policy learning, yet remain fundamentally reactive, mapping current observations and language to actions without explicit forward prediction of world dynamics. Existing visual foresight methods predict future visual states but lack explicit motion guidance: they show where to go but not how to get there. We argue that future feature prediction and sparse point tracking are naturally complementary: the former provides the goal state, while the latter captures the continuous motion path toward it. We propose FoMoVLA, a framework that augments VLA representations with explicit spatio-temporal supervision by jointly learning future feature foresight and sparse 2D point tracking, enhancing the continuous action policy. FoMoVLA introduces compact foresight tokens to decode future feature states, decodes sparse temporal 2D point trajectories to model compact geometric motion, and couples both through a lightweight future-conditioned cross-attention module that enables consistent reasoning between anticipated states and point dynamics. Extensive experiments on LIBERO, RoboCasa GR-1 Tabletop, and LIBERO-Plus demonstrate state-of-the-art performance and strong zero-shot generalization. Project page is available at https://liauto-research.github.io/FoMoVLA.

AI.tldr: FoMoVLA is a VLA framework that jointly learns future feature prediction and sparse 2D point tracking to enhance action policy learning, achieving SOTA results on LIBERO, RoboCasa GR-1 Tabletop, and LIBERO-Plus with strong zero-shot generalization.
AI.motivation: Existing VLA models are reactive without forward world dynamics prediction, and visual foresight methods lack explicit motion guidance (showing where to go but not how).
AI.method: FoMoVLA augments VLA with future feature foresight (via compact foresight tokens) and sparse 2D point tracking, coupled through a future-conditioned cross-attention module for consistent reasoning between anticipated states and point dynamics.
AI.result: State-of-the-art performance on LIBERO, RoboCasa GR-1 Tabletop, and LIBERO-Plus benchmarks with strong zero-shot generalization.
AI.conclusion: Jointly learning future feature prediction and sparse point tracking is complementary and effective for enhancing continuous action policy in visuomotor tasks.

title: MathCoPilot: An Interactive System for Human-AI Symbiotic Paradigm of Mathematical Research
summary: Existing LLM-based theorem provers have achieved impressive results on formal mathematics benchmarks, yet they remain confined to acting as autonomous agents that prove a stated proposition. In this paper, we propose MathCoPilot, a human-in-the-loop system that embodies a new human--AI symbiotic paradigm for mathematical research, in which the mathematician steers the high-level mathematical direction while AI agents carry out the detailed formalization and proof work under continuous human guidance. MathCoPilot unifies three core capabilities: (1) an interactive workbench where the mathematician and AI agents collaborate through a living proof blueprint that decomposes a proof into navigable steps the human can directly inspect, direct, and refine; (2) automated proving skill orchestration with adaptive knowledge base search and Lean-integrated iterative verification; and (3) topic-driven paper retrieval and automated formalization into a verified Lean knowledge base. Using MathCoPilot, we systematically compare four state-of-the-art LLMs, including Gemini~3.1~Pro, GPT-5.4, and Claude~Opus~4.7, on a FormalMATH subset and on two real PDE theorems requiring deep domain expertise, evaluating their ability to produce verified Lean~4 proofs and to identify errors in deliberately incorrect proofs. Our results show that while current models can handle undergraduate-level problems with high success rates under favorable autoformalization conditions, substantial challenges remain for domain-specific theorems requiring genuine mathematical understanding.

AI.tldr: MathCoPilot is a human-in-the-loop system for formal theorem proving that unifies an interactive workbench, automated proving skill orchestration with Lean verification, and topic-driven paper retrieval. It evaluates four LLMs on formal math benchmarks and real PDE theorems, showing strong performance on undergraduate problems but significant challenges remain for domain-specific theorems requiring deep understanding.
AI.motivation: Existing LLM-based theorem provers are confined to acting as autonomous agents that prove stated propositions, lacking human collaboration. This limits their utility in real mathematical research where human guidance is essential for high-level direction.
AI.method: MathCoPilot combines three core capabilities: (1) an interactive workbench with a living proof blueprint for human-AI collaboration; (2) automated proving skill orchestration with adaptive knowledge base search and Lean-integrated iterative verification; (3) topic-driven paper retrieval and automated formalization into a verified Lean knowledge base. Four LLMs (Gemini 3.1 Pro, GPT-5.4, Claude Opus 4.7) were evaluated on FormalMATH subset and two real PDE theorems.
AI.result: Current models handle undergraduate-level problems with high success rates under favorable autoformalization conditions, but substantial challenges remain for domain-specific theorems requiring genuine mathematical understanding.
AI.conclusion: MathCoPilot introduces a new human-AI symbiotic paradigm for mathematical research where mathematicians steer high-level direction while AI handles formalization. The system demonstrates the potential and current limitations of LLMs in collaborative theorem proving.

title: Angular Gaussian Supervised Contrastive Learning for Long-Tailed Electrocardiogram Arrhythmia Diagnosis
summary: Long-tailed label distributions reduce the reliability of deep learning for electrocardiogram (ECG) arrhythmia diagnosis, particularly for clinically important but rare abnormalities. Existing rebalancing and logit adjustment methods mainly address class frequency while overlooking direction-dependent morphological variability across ECG classes. This study proposes Angular Gaussian Supervised Contrastive Learning (AG-SCL) for long-tailed multi-label ECG diagnosis. AG-SCL integrates three components into a unified framework: an Angular Gaussian contrastive branch that models full-covariance class uncertainty on unit-normalized embeddings, Adaptive Logit Adjustment that learns bounded label-state-specific prior corrections instead of fixed frequency-based margins, and tail-aware augmentation that generates morphology-preserving views while protecting the 7-25 Hz QRS-dominant band. The method was evaluated on the public PTB-XL benchmark and a nocturnal ECG dataset comprising 1317 hours of recordings from 141 subjects. AG-SCL achieved the best macro-level performance on both datasets. On PTB-XL, it obtained a balanced accuracy of 0.838, sensitivity of 0.709, specificity of 0.968, mean average precision of 0.495, and TPR at 5% FPR of 0.778. On Noc-ECG, the corresponding values were 0.918, 0.889, 0.947, 0.488, and 0.900. The largest gains occurred in rare or morphologically unstable rhythm classes, while ablation studies confirmed the contributions of full-covariance modelling, Adaptive Logit Adjustment, and tail-aware augmentation. AG-SCL improves long-tailed ECG diagnosis by combining prior calibration with anisotropic representation learning, enhancing sensitivity to rare arrhythmias while maintaining clinically relevant specificity. Our code is available at: https://github.com/Open-EXG/AG-SCL-for-Long-Tailed-ECG.

AI.tldr: AG-SCL is a framework combining Angular Gaussian contrastive learning, Adaptive Logit Adjustment, and tail-aware augmentation to improve long-tailed multi-label ECG arrhythmia diagnosis, achieving state-of-the-art results on PTB-XL and Noc-ECG datasets with particular gains in rare rhythm classes.
AI.motivation: Long-tailed label distributions reduce reliability of deep learning for ECG arrhythmia diagnosis, especially for clinically important but rare abnormalities. Existing methods mainly address class frequency while overlooking direction-dependent morphological variability across ECG classes.
AI.method: AG-SCL integrates three components: (1) Angular Gaussian contrastive branch modeling full-covariance class uncertainty on unit-normalized embeddings; (2) Adaptive Logit Adjustment learning bounded label-state-specific prior corrections instead of fixed frequency-based margins; (3) Tail-aware augmentation generating morphology-preserving views while protecting the 7-25 Hz QRS-dominant band.
AI.result: On PTB-XL: balanced accuracy 0.838, sensitivity 0.709, specificity 0.968, mAP 0.495, TPR@5%FPR 0.778. On Noc-ECG: 0.918, 0.889, 0.947, 0.488, 0.900 respectively. Largest gains in rare or morphologically unstable rhythm classes.
AI.conclusion: AG-SCL improves long-tailed ECG diagnosis by combining prior calibration with anisotropic representation learning, enhancing sensitivity to rare arrhythmias while maintaining clinically relevant specificity.

title: On the Disagreement in Perturbation-based xAI -- Benchmarking Perturbation Choices for Flood Detection from SAR Images
summary: Perturbation-based xAI methods are widely used to analyze the behavior and predictions of deep learning models. By altering input regions and measuring the resulting changes in class probabilities with respect to the original image, they assign relevance scores and generate heatmaps that reflect each region's contribution to the prediction. Despite their apparent simplicity, however, perturbation-based methods are sensitive to parameter choices. In this work, we focus on two key parameters of the perturbation pipeline, namely the patch geometry, including the size and shape of the perturbed regions, and the perturbation type, defined by the replacement scheme. Grounded in the use case of flood detection from Synthetic Aperture Radar imagery, we conduct a comprehensive investigation of how relevance estimation changes under different perturbation settings. Beyond visual inspection of the resulting relevance maps, we evaluate their consistency across perturbation strategies and their faithfulness to the model's reasoning. We demonstrate how different perturbation choices can steer the resulting relevance maps, yielding ambiguous and even contradictory explanations. Our findings emphasize the importance of methodological settings in perturbation-based xAI. They underscore the need to carefully inspect and evaluate perturbation choices and to treat them as an integral part when interpreting explanations, ensuring a robust understanding of both the explanations and model predictions.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how parameter choices (patch geometry and perturbation type) in perturbation-based xAI methods significantly affect relevance maps, leading to ambiguous and contradictory explanations in the context of flood detection from SAR imagery.
AI.motivation: Perturbation-based xAI methods are widely used but are sensitive to parameter choices, yet the impact of these choices on explanation reliability is understudied. The authors aim to systematically evaluate how different perturbation settings affect relevance estimation consistency and faithfulness.
AI.method: The authors conduct a comprehensive investigation using flood detection from Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery as a use case. They vary two key parameters: (1) patch geometry (size and shape of perturbed regions) and (2) perturbation type (replacement scheme). They evaluate relevance maps via visual inspection, consistency across strategies, and faithfulness to model reasoning.
AI.result: Different perturbation choices can produce ambiguous and even contradictory explanations. The consistency and faithfulness of relevance maps vary significantly depending on the perturbation settings, demonstrating that parameter choices strongly steer the resulting explanations.
AI.conclusion: Methodological settings in perturbation-based xAI are critical and must be carefully inspected and evaluated. Perturbation choices should be treated as an integral part of interpreting explanations to ensure robust understanding of both the explanations and model predictions.

title: SportD: Can VLMs Physically Strategize?
summary: Vision--language models have become increasingly capable of interpreting visual scenes, but it remains unclear whether they can use information to make strategically effective decisions. We investigate this question in soccer, where models observe the seconds preceding an on-ball decision and must choose whether to shoot or pass to a specific teammate. Unlike conventional visual-understanding tasks, soccer enables decisions to be evaluated quantitatively by estimating the value of every available action. We introduce SportD, a benchmark comprising 478 on-ball decisions from the 2022 FIFA World Cup. Each model choice is evaluated against a possession-value model that estimates the action that most increases the attacking team's probability of scoring, allowing us to measure both optimal-action accuracy and the value forfeited by suboptimal decisions. Across three frontier VLMs, the best selects the highest-valued action on 31.4% of events, compared with 38.9% for the professional players, and all models incur significantly greater regret. Further analysis reveals a systematic preference for lower-variance and lower-reward actions: VLMs shoot less often and select substantially less progressive passes than either the optimal policy or the real players. The models also reproduce the player's specific action above chance even when that action is suboptimal, suggesting partial imitation of familiar play patterns rather than consistent evaluation of counterfactual alternatives. SportD provides a value-grounded testbed for measuring physical strategic reasoning in VLMs.

AI.tldr: Vision-language models (VLMs) struggle with strategic decision-making in soccer: they achieve lower optimal-action accuracy (31.4% vs. 38.9% for professionals) and exhibit systematic biases toward lower-risk, lower-reward actions, suggesting partial imitation rather than genuine counterfactual reasoning.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether vision-language models can use visual information to make strategically effective decisions, moving beyond conventional visual understanding tasks to quantitatively evaluate decision quality using a possession-value model.
AI.method: Introduced SportD benchmark with 478 on-ball decisions from 2022 FIFA World Cup; each model choice evaluated against a possession-value model estimating the action that most increases scoring probability, measuring optimal-action accuracy and regret (value forfeited by suboptimal choices).
AI.result: Best VLM selects highest-valued action on 31.4% vs. 38.9% for professionals; VLMs show systematic preference for lower-variance/lower-reward actions, shoot less often, select less progressive passes, and partially imitate player-specific actions even when suboptimal.
AI.conclusion: SportD provides a value-grounded testbed for measuring physical strategic reasoning in VLMs, revealing that current models lack consistent counterfactual evaluation and instead rely on partial imitation of observed patterns.

title: Beyond Entropy: Correctness-Aware Advantage Shaping via Contrastive Policy Optimization
summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) commonly uses entropy for advantage shaping. However, entropy cannot distinguish useful uncertainty from detrimental confusion, limiting its effectiveness as a correctness signal. We propose Contrastive Policy Optimization (CPO), which uses token-level contrastive disagreement between reference-guided and vanilla generation distributions for correctness-aware advantage shaping. Both theoretical and empirical results show that this disagreement reliably indicates token-level correctness. We further show that On-policy Distillation is a special case of CPO, where the posterior distribution is instantiated by an external teacher model. CPO also resolves the zero-advantage problem. Experiments on in-domain and out-of-domain benchmarks demonstrate that CPO substantially outperforms entropy-based RLVR methods while maintaining strong generalization. Further analysis shows that correct and incorrect responses naturally support exploration and exploitation respectively, and balancing both leads to the best performance.

AI.tldr: CPO uses contrastive disagreement between reference-guided and vanilla generation distributions for advantage shaping, outperforming entropy-based RLVR methods.
AI.motivation: Entropy-based advantage shaping in RLVR cannot distinguish useful uncertainty from detrimental confusion, limiting its effectiveness as a correctness signal.
AI.method: Proposes Contrastive Policy Optimization (CPO) using token-level contrastive disagreement between reference-guided and vanilla generation distributions for correctness-aware advantage shaping.
AI.result: CPO substantially outperforms entropy-based RLVR methods on in-domain and out-of-domain benchmarks while maintaining strong generalization.
AI.conclusion: Correct and incorrect responses naturally support exploration and exploitation respectively; balancing both leads to best performance. CPO also resolves the zero-advantage problem.

title: Clean-Reference Streaming Detection of Lens Occlusion and Photometric Transitions for Camera Tamper Monitoring
summary: A surveillance camera is an image sensor whose silent physical degradation invalidates every downstream consumer of its data. In-situ integrity alarms for such vision sensors require low false-alarm rates, bounded computation, and diagnosable behavior under nuisance illumination changes. This paper studies a deliberately narrow streaming integrity monitor for two low-cost sensor-fault signatures: texture-collapsing lens occlusion and abrupt photometric scene transition. The detector compares sampled luminance and local-gradient statistics with a clean-only sliding reference, applies coarse-grid structured-light rejection and mode/rapid-brightness suppression, and emits at most one notification per tamper episode. We formalize the decision predicates and derive a consistency rule for when rapid-brightness suppression makes the scene-transition path unreachable. On 320 in-scope controlled sequences, the default state machine attains 0.800 F1 and 0.822 balanced accuracy (significantly better paired correctness than the strongest baseline, though the F1 margin is not statistically resolved); on a magnitude-swept public audit it attains the highest partial AUC under a 5\% false-alarm budget, and a separate extended-stress FPR-constrained sweep reaches 0.925 recall at 0.025 false-positive rate. Public Xiph, Bremen IoT, and UHCTD diagnostics show the fixed predicates preserve low false alarms while recall concentrates inside the declared envelope (UHCTD in-scope covered recall 0.667 versus 0.016 out of scope), and a 9.09-camera-hour verified-negative public audit records zero false alarms. The method is best interpreted as an auditable sensor-health subsystem rather than a universal camera-tamper classifier.

AI.tldr: A lightweight, streaming integrity monitor for surveillance cameras detects two specific sensor faults (lens occlusion and abrupt scene transitions) using luminance and gradient statistics with a sliding reference, achieving high precision and low false-alarm rates while remaining auditable and diagnosable.
AI.motivation: Physical degradation of surveillance cameras silently invalidates downstream data consumers; existing tamper detection systems suffer from high false-alarm rates under nuisance illumination changes and lack diagnosable, bounded-computation behavior.
AI.method: Compares sampled luminance and local-gradient statistics against a clean-only sliding reference; employs coarse-grid structured-light rejection and mode/rapid-brightness suppression; formalized as a state machine emitting at most one notification per tamper episode with consistency rules for unreachable transition paths.
AI.result: 0.800 F1 and 0.822 balanced accuracy on 320 in-scope sequences; highest partial AUC under 5% false-alarm budget on magnitude-swept public audit; 0.925 recall at 0.025 FPR on extended-stress test; zero false alarms on 9.09 camera-hour verified-negative audit; in-scope recall 0.667 vs 0.016 out-of-scope on UHCTD.
AI.conclusion: The method is best interpreted as an auditable sensor-health subsystem rather than a universal camera-tamper classifier, offering statistically significant correctness improvements over baselines with bounded computation and low false-alarm rates.

title: Action QFormer: Structured Representation Shaping under Action Supervision in Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: Action supervision in vision-language-action (VLA) models is often treated as a downstream objective for learning action prediction. In this paper, we study it instead as a force that shapes inherited multimodal representations. We show that this shaping has a dual effect: it is necessary for forming action-compatible representations, but when action supervision is applied too directly to the inherited multimodal pathway, it can also destabilize representations that support language-side processing and object grounding. To address this tension, we introduce Action QFormer, a query-based action-facing interface that uses instruction-conditioned queries to reorganize inherited multimodal information into action-facing representations before downstream action generation. In zero-shot sim-to-real navigation, Action QFormer improves average closed-loop task success from 18.8% to 56.3%, raises fixed-instruction action-generation correctness from 22.5% to 75.5%, and nearly eliminates out-of-distribution instruction generations. Further analyses show that Action QFormer changes how action supervision shapes inherited multimodal representations, reducing broad upstream rewriting while preserving targeted and sometimes constructive action-supervised adaptation. These results suggest that improving VLA performance requires not only stronger pretrained backbones, but also better ways of selecting and organizing inherited multimodal information while controlling how it is shaped under action supervision.

AI.tldr: Action QFormer is a query-based interface that reorganizes inherited multimodal representations before action generation in VLA models, preventing destabilization of language/grounding capabilities while improving task success from 18.8% to 56.3% in zero-shot sim-to-real navigation.
AI.motivation: Action supervision in VLA models has a dual effect: it is necessary for forming action-compatible representations but can destabilize representations supporting language processing and object grounding when applied too directly to the inherited multimodal pathway.
AI.method: Action QFormer, a query-based action-facing interface that uses instruction-conditioned queries to reorganize inherited multimodal information into action-facing representations before downstream action generation.
AI.result: Zero-shot sim-to-real navigation: closed-loop task success improved from 18.8% to 56.3%; fixed-instruction action-generation correctness from 22.5% to 75.5%; nearly eliminated out-of-distribution instruction generations.
AI.conclusion: Improving VLA performance requires not only stronger pretrained backbones but also better ways of selecting and organizing inherited multimodal information while controlling how it is shaped under action supervision.

title: PolyQ: Codesigning End-to-End Quantization Framework for Scalable Edge CPU LLM Inference
summary: CPUs are the most universal target for on-device LLM inference, but existing low-bit quantization methods offer either coarse operating points or fine-grained mixed precision that is difficult to execute efficiently on CPUs. We present PolyQ, a CPU-oriented compiler/quantization co-design for activation-aware channel-wise bit allocation under a user-specified average-bit budget. PolyQ assigns per-channel bit-widths from $\{2,3,4,8,16\}$, then uses a compile-time model compiler to permute and cluster channels into bit-homogeneous blocks, generate SIMD- and LUT-compatible kernels, and merge compatible permutations across operators to keep layout regularization off the runtime path. This turns fine-grained budget fitting into a practical fractional-bit deployment method for CPU-only inference. Across Falcon-H1-3B, Llama2-13B, and Qwen3-32B on WikiText-2, PolyQ provides stable quality scaling from 3--6\,b and improves perplexity by 2.4--32.1\% over prior methods at a 3\,b target. End-to-end measurements on three representative CPUs -- workstation, laptop, and mobile -- show that compiler layout regularization reduces activation reorder traffic by up to 70.8\%, prefill latency and decode throughput scale nearly proportionally with the configured bit budget, and energy/token overhead stays below 2\% relative to an optimized LUT-based back-end. These results show that fractional-bit CPU deployment is practical, predictable, and energy-efficient across diverse edge targets.

AI.tldr: PolyQ is a CPU-oriented compiler/quantization co-design that enables practical fractional-bit deployment for on-device LLM inference by assigning per-channel bit-widths from {2,3,4,8,16} and using a compile-time model compiler to permute/cluster channels into bit-homogeneous blocks with SIMD/LUT kernels, achieving 2.4-32.1% perplexity improvement over prior methods and up to 70.8% reduction in activation reorder traffic.
AI.motivation: CPUs are the most universal target for on-device LLM inference, but existing low-bit quantization methods offer either coarse operating points or fine-grained mixed precision that is difficult to execute efficiently on CPUs.
AI.method: PolyQ uses activation-aware channel-wise bit allocation under a user-specified average-bit budget, assigns per-channel bit-widths from {2,3,4,8,16}, employs a compile-time model compiler to permute and cluster channels into bit-homogeneous blocks, generates SIMD- and LUT-compatible kernels, and merges compatible permutations across operators to keep layout regularization off the runtime path.
AI.result: Across Falcon-H1-3B, Llama2-13B, and Qwen3-32B on WikiText-2, PolyQ provides stable quality scaling from 3-6b and improves perplexity by 2.4-32.1% over prior methods at a 3b target. End-to-end measurements show compiler layout regularization reduces activation reorder traffic by up to 70.8%, prefill latency and decode throughput scale nearly proportionally with the configured bit budget, and energy/token overhead stays below 2%.
AI.conclusion: Fractional-bit CPU deployment is practical, predictable, and energy-efficient across diverse edge targets.

title: Rare Concept Generation via Counterfactual Inference in Diffusion Models
comment: Comments: 17 pages, 15 figures, to appear at ACM Multimedia 2026
summary: Rare concept generation focuses on synthesizing customized images conditioned on text prompts that describe objects with unusual attributes. Previous works failed to align the generated images with rare concepts, resulting in incorrect attribute rendering or inconsistent composition of concepts. Such failures, as we observed, stem from the inherent common knowledge bias in the training stage of diffusion models, where objects are strongly associated with their common attributes, making it difficult to break these associations when generating rare concepts. To address such challenges, in this paper, we propose a novel Counterfactual Inference-based Diffusion approach, dubbed CI-Diff. CI-Diff blocks the interference of the model's inherent common knowledge bias and utilizes the Natural Direct Effect to capture the independent influence of the text prompt of rare concepts on image generation so that decoupling the unusual attributes from the rare concepts. To this end, we reformulate the classifier-free guidance mechanism to highlight the atypical attributes. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to introduce causal inference into the rare concept generation task. Extensive experiments on the RareBench benchmark validate the superiority of CI-Diff over state-of-the-art diffusion models. Our code can be accessed from https://github.com/200204jzy/CI-Diff.

AI.tldr: CI-Diff is a counterfactual inference-based diffusion model that addresses rare concept generation by blocking common knowledge bias and using Natural Direct Effect to decouple unusual attributes, outperforming SOTA methods on RareBench.
AI.motivation: Existing diffusion models fail to generate rare concepts (objects with unusual attributes) due to inherent common knowledge bias from training, where objects are strongly tied to their common attributes, causing incorrect attribute rendering or inconsistent composition.
AI.method: CI-Diff employs counterfactual inference to block the interference of common knowledge bias, uses Natural Direct Effect to capture the independent influence of rare concept text prompts on generation, and reformulates classifier-free guidance to highlight atypical attributes.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on the RareBench benchmark demonstrate the superiority of CI-Diff over state-of-the-art diffusion models in generating rare concepts.
AI.conclusion: CI-Diff is the first to introduce causal inference into rare concept generation, effectively decoupling unusual attributes from rare concepts by mitigating common knowledge bias.

title: Analytic Abduction: Causal Decomposition and Governed Commitment for Human--AI Coordination
summary: Abductive reasoning operates in two directions. The synthetic mode builds explanations from available hypotheses; the analytic mode, conversely, identifies the latent factors whose interaction accounts for a complex observed state. This paper develops the analytic mode as a non-greedy, risk-sensitive discipline of commitment, in which candidate factors coexist and interact, resolving into committed conclusions only when explicit governance conditions are met. The formal core is the $κ$-$τ$ apparatus: $κ$ encodes the epistemic interaction among hypotheses, and $τ$ sets a commitment threshold calibrated to the decision's stakes. The central contribution is the causal cluster, a structured object recording which latent factors participate in a decomposition, with what weights and interaction structure, together with a two-level architecture (intra-cluster $κ^*$, inter-cluster $κ^{**}$) that guards against causal misattribution. Demonstrated in epidemiological crisis decomposition and adversarial cyber threat analysis, the framework's contribution to human-AI reasoning is the legibility of suspended decomposition as a shared coordination object, providing structural resistance to premature convergence. In practice, the decision-maker is handed not a single imposed answer but the competing explanatory scenarios, weighted by plausibility and paired with the evidence that would resolve between them, so that sound action is possible even before the ambiguity is resolved.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the κ-τ framework for analytic abductive reasoning, where latent causal factors coexist and interact until explicit governance conditions are met, demonstrated in epidemiology and cybersecurity contexts.
AI.motivation: To formalize analytic abductive reasoning as a non-greedy, risk-sensitive discipline where conclusions are deferred until explicit governance conditions are met, addressing the problem of premature convergence in complex causal decomposition.
AI.method: The κ-τ apparatus, where κ encodes epistemic interaction among hypotheses and τ sets a commitment threshold calibrated to decision stakes. Includes causal clusters with two-level architecture (intra-cluster κ*, inter-cluster κ**) to prevent causal misattribution.
AI.result: Demonstrated in epidemiological crisis decomposition and adversarial cyber threat analysis; produces legible suspended decompositions that serve as shared coordination objects between human and AI, providing structural resistance to premature convergence.
AI.conclusion: The framework delivers competing explanatory scenarios weighted by plausibility with evidence needed for resolution, enabling sound action even before ambiguity is resolved, rather than imposing a single answer.

title: TIDE: Trustworthy and Interpretable Battery Degradation Estimation with Contextual Learning and Symbolic Distillation
summary: Battery health estimation is fundamental for battery management in battery-powered systems, where inaccurate health states may affect control, maintenance, and service life. It becomes even more critical in intelligent connected systems, where estimation errors can propagate across interconnected devices and downstream decisions. In this paper, we propose TIDE, a trustworthy and interpretable battery degradation estimator for reliable battery health estimation. TIDE jointly considers accuracy, trustworthiness, and interpretability, which are all essential for practical deployment and downstream decision making. To realize these objectives, TIDE combines battery-domain knowledge with operational measurements in a three-component backbone. A knowledge-guided degradation prior promotes trustworthy estimation, a monotone residual component provides interpretable aging-consistent refinement, and a contextual learning component captures battery-specific operational effects for improved accuracy. The trained backbone is then distilled into a compact symbolic surrogate that provides a concise model-level interpretation of its learned estimation logic. Experiments show that TIDE achieves strong estimation accuracy, improving overall estimation fidelity by an average of 19.7% over representative baselines. Its knowledge-guided prior and monotone residual modelling substantially reduce aging-consistency violations, supporting trustworthy estimation. Meanwhile, the backbone enables component-level interpretation, while symbolic distillation provides a compact model-level representation of the learned estimation logic. These results support the practical use of TIDE for battery health monitoring and decision support in intelligent connected systems.

AI.tldr: TIDE is a trustworthy and interpretable battery degradation estimator that jointly optimizes accuracy, trustworthiness, and interpretability via a three-component backbone (knowledge-guided prior, monotone residual, contextual learning) plus symbolic distillation, achieving 19.7% improvement over baselines.
AI.motivation: Battery health estimation is critical for management in battery-powered systems, especially in intelligent connected systems where estimation errors can propagate across interconnected devices. Existing methods lack joint consideration of accuracy, trustworthiness, and interpretability, all essential for practical deployment and downstream decision making.
AI.method: TIDE combines battery-domain knowledge with operational measurements in a three-component backbone: (1) a knowledge-guided degradation prior for trustworthy estimation, (2) a monotone residual component for interpretable aging-consistent refinement, and (3) a contextual learning component for battery-specific operational effects. The trained backbone is distilled into a compact symbolic surrogate for model-level interpretability.
AI.result: TIDE improves overall estimation fidelity by an average of 19.7% over representative baselines. Its knowledge-guided prior and monotone residual modelling substantially reduce aging-consistency violations, supporting trustworthy estimation. The backbone enables component-level interpretation, while symbolic distillation provides a compact model-level representation.
AI.conclusion: TIDE achieves strong estimation accuracy (19.7% improvement over baselines), reduces aging-consistency violations for trustworthiness, and provides both component-level (backbone) and model-level (symbolic surrogate) interpretability, supporting its practical use for battery health monitoring and decision support in intelligent connected systems.

title: TAMF-VTON: Texture-Aware Mask-Free Virtual Try-On via High-Fidelity Image Synthesis
summary: Recent diffusion-based virtual try-on (VTON) methods remain limited by their reliance on segmentation masks, insufficient preservation of fine-grained textures, and limited support for arbitrary multi-garment compositions. Consequently, existing approaches still face significant challenges in real-world e-commerce deployment. We present TAMF-VTON, a texture-aware, mask-free framework that enables high-fidelity image synthesis under practical unconstrained conditions. Our method requires no human parsing or inpainting masks at inference time and supports diverse garment styles, categories, and quantities, enabling the simultaneous transfer of multiple items while preserving body structure and intricate texture details. This is achieved through a unified generative pipeline with three key components: (1) a lightweight Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) adaptation scheme that enables efficient fine-tuning without compromising the base model's general editing capabilities; (2) a frequency-domain supervision mechanism that explicitly optimizes high-frequency spectral consistency to preserve high-fidelity textures; and (3) a robust data curation pipeline employing an adaptive inpainting strategy to simulate the inverse VTON process for high-quality training pair generation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both quantitative metrics and perceptual quality. Optimized for efficiency, the model achieves inference in under 15 seconds per image on an NVIDIA RTX 4090 with INT4 quantization. By combining mask-free operation, flexible multi-garment composition, faithful texture preservation, and efficient inference on consumer hardware, TAMF-VTON demonstrates a commercially viable solution for scalable deployment in real-world digital fashion scenarios. The project is available at https://www.style3d.ai/ai-photoshoot/virtual-clothing-try-on.

AI.tldr: TAMF-VTON is a texture-aware, mask-free diffusion framework for virtual try-on that supports multi-garment composition without segmentation masks, uses MoE fine-tuning, frequency-domain texture supervision, and an adaptive inpainting data pipeline, achieving high-fidelity results in under 15 seconds per image on consumer GPUs.
AI.motivation: Existing diffusion-based VTON methods are limited by reliance on segmentation masks, poor preservation of fine-grained textures, and lack of support for arbitrary multi-garment compositions, hindering real-world e-commerce deployment.
AI.method: A unified generative pipeline with three key components: (1) lightweight Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) adaptation for efficient fine-tuning; (2) frequency-domain supervision optimizing high-frequency spectral consistency for texture fidelity; (3) a robust data curation pipeline using adaptive inpainting to simulate inverse VTON for high-quality training pair generation.
AI.result: Outperforms state-of-the-art methods in quantitative metrics and perceptual quality; achieves inference in under 15 seconds per image on an NVIDIA RTX 4090 with INT4 quantization.
AI.conclusion: By combining mask-free operation, flexible multi-garment composition, faithful texture preservation, and efficient inference on consumer hardware, TAMF-VTON demonstrates a commercially viable solution for scalable deployment in real-world digital fashion.

title: Trajectory-Aware Flow Matching for Topology Optimisation
summary: Topology optimisation (TO) often requires repeated finite element analysis and sensitivity-based material updates, which can be costly when multiple candidate designs are needed under varying physical and design conditions. Generative TO offers a route to rapid design exploration, but existing models may rely on adversarial training, long reverse-diffusion sampling, or external guidance to maintain structural feasibility and physical consistency.
